seo.title: Help for people experiencing homelessness in Vancouver - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help in Vancouver for people experiencing homelessness: shelters, food, showers, health care, benefits, jobs, documents and specialist support.

page.heading: Vancouver — help for people experiencing homelessness

notice.text: Hours, eligibility and spaces can change.

Call before travelling when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, meal, payment, appointment, document or job. BC211's Vancouver shelter list is the best starting point for current bed and mat information.

content.text: When asking for help, say where you are, your age, whether you have a safe place tonight, and whether children, a partner, a pet, large belongings, accessibility needs or urgent health needs are involved. Ask the worker to explain the intake process before you travel.
No Home Help is not part of the City, Province or any service provider. Verify information before travelling.
Phone:
. Call for a serious medical emergency, suspected overdose, fire, violence or a crime in progress.

Give the exact address, nearest intersection or visible landmark. Say what happened and whether the person is conscious and breathing. If it is safe, stay on the line and follow the operator's instructions.
Emergency guidance — City of Vancouver

items.name: BC211 — shelter, food and local services

content.text: Call or text:
. Current navigator hours are 9am to 9pm on weekdays, excluding statutory holidays. The website can be searched at any time.

Ask for a shelter that fits your age, gender, household, accessibility and pet needs. BC211 can also search for food, health, legal, financial, newcomer and transport services. It cannot reserve or guarantee a bed.
BC211
Drop-in:
392 Powell Street
Office:
Outreach cell:
. Drop-in is first come, first served, Monday to Friday, 9am to 4pm, except statutory holidays.

City outreach workers can help with shelter, housing applications, income benefits, identification, health referrals, clothing, detox and harm-reduction supplies. The team also conducts street outreach.
Homelessness Services Outreach Team — City of Vancouver

items.name: VictimLinkBC — violence, crime and human trafficking

content.text: Call or text:
, 24 hours. The service is confidential, toll-free and multilingual.

VictimLinkBC can provide immediate support and referrals to transition houses, victim services, counselling and legal or safety-planning resources. You do not need to be certain that a crime occurred before contacting the service. Call 911 for immediate danger.
VictimLinkBC — Government of British Columbia

BC211 lists beds and mats for adults, women, youth and families, with filters for pets, large belongings and wheelchair access. The list is normally updated twice on weekdays, at 11:30am and 7:30pm, excluding statutory holidays.
Before travelling:
check the intake notes and call the shelter. A listing may say full, may change after the update or may require an in-person draw, referral or assessment.
Vancouver shelter list — BC211

The provincial map shows year-round, temporary, winter and Extreme Weather Response shelters, plus drop-in centres. It shows locations and program information but does not guarantee that a bed is free.
Housing Assistance:
in the Lower Mainland or
elsewhere in British Columbia.
Emergency Shelter Program — BC Housing

items.name: Yukon Shelter — adults of any gender

content.text: Address:
2088 Yukon Street
Shelter desk:
. The year-round shelter serves adults aged 19 and older. BC211 currently lists it as pet-friendly and wheelchair accessible.
Call for current space and intake instructions. Pet capacity, storage and accessibility arrangements can still vary.
Yukon Housing Centre — Lookout Housing and Health Society

items.name: Union Gospel Mission men's emergency shelter

content.text: Address:
601 East Hastings Street; enter from Princess Avenue
Reception:
, open 24 hours. The men's shelter operates year-round and provides a place to sleep, showers, laundry and overnight storage.
Contact reception before going to ask about eligibility, current space and intake. The same site has outreach staff, meals and a clothing room.
Get help — Union Gospel Mission
Address:
555 Homer Street
Phone:
. The Salvation Army describes a year-round, wheelchair-accessible shelter with three meals a day and other supports. The program is alcohol- and drug-free.
Call about current eligibility, family composition and bed availability before travelling.
Belkin House emergency shelter — Salvation Army
Address:
412 East Cordova Street
Phones:
or
. The Downtown Eastside Women's Centre lists this emergency shelter as open 24 hours, every day.
Contact the shelter about current space and intake. The service is for self-identified women; the provider also operates drop-in centres and other shelter sites.
Emergency shelter — Downtown Eastside Women's Centre
Address:
340 Alexander Street
Participant phone:
. WISH operates a 24-hour shelter for women and gender-diverse street-based sex workers, with food, showers, laundry, clothing and harm-reduction supplies.
Call about eligibility and current intake. Some beds are for short respite and others for longer stays while housing is sought.
WISH Shelter
Crisis program:
1280 Seymour Street;
drop-in:
1302 Seymour Street
Phone:
Toll-free:
. Youth can self-refer for free shelter and services; no parent or social worker is required to make the referral.
Call about the Crisis Program or Sanctuary and explain any health, safety or substance-use needs. Admission depends on the appropriate program and available space.
Get help — Covenant House Vancouver
Address:
1138 Burrard Street
Call or text:
. The low-barrier drop-in is open 24 hours and accepts youth with pets, substance use or mental-health challenges.

The regular overnight shelter has 12 beds for ages 19 to 24. Current intake is in person: speak to staff from 8pm to 8:30pm for the 9pm draw; no intake after 2am. Check with staff because the process can change.
Directions drop-in and overnight shelter
Ho'-kee-melh Kloshe Lum:
1015 East Hastings Street

The Vancouver Aboriginal Friendship Centre Society operates a structured 90-day shelter and transition program for adults aged 19 and older, with housing navigation, meals, laundry, cultural programming and other supports.
Access is by referral only
through an emergency shelter or community health provider; walk-in admission is not accepted. Pets may be considered case by case.
Shelter program — Vancouver Aboriginal Friendship Centre Society

Ask the worker to check another site, explain the next update time and identify any winter or extreme-weather space. Do not assume a different site accepts the same age, household, pet, mobility device or belongings.
Check the BC211 live list again later, call or text 211 during navigator hours, or contact City outreach. Call 911 if remaining outside creates an immediate medical emergency.
Check current spaces — BC211
Address:
601 East Hastings Street; enter from Princess Avenue
Meal tickets are available 15 minutes before service. Lunch is served every day at 11am. Dinner is served Monday to Friday at 6pm and Saturday and Sunday at 4pm.
Schedules can change on holidays or during operational disruptions. Contact reception at
if travelling a long distance.
Meal times — Union Gospel Mission

items.name: The Door Is Open — Catholic drop-in and meals

content.text: Address:
255 Dunlevy Avenue
Phone:
. Free lunch is listed at 11am Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday; 12 noon Sunday. Wednesday has a women's breakfast at 8:30am and women's lunch at 11:30am.
The drop-in also provides clothing, counselling and referrals. Confirm the schedule before going, especially on holidays.
The Door Is Open

items.name: Downtown Eastside Women's Centre — daily meals

content.text: Address:
302 Columbia Street
Phone:
. Breakfast is listed at 10am, lunch from 12:30pm to 1:45pm and snacks from 3pm to 3:30pm every day.

The low-barrier centre serves women and also offers clothing, showers, washrooms, toiletries, mail, phone and computer access. It opens at 11am on Wednesdays and may close one Wednesday each month on income-assistance payment day.
302 Columbia Street — Downtown Eastside Women's Centre
Registration:
or reception@foodbank.bc.ca. Registration appointments are required; walk-in registration is not offered.

Bring government photo ID, recent proof of an address in the service area and identification for dependants. A new client who arrives at a distribution site with only their own ID can receive food on the first visit, but must complete registration for ongoing weekly access.
Food bank registration
Current locations and schedule

items.name: Carnegie, Gathering Place and Evelyne Saller cafeterias

content.text: City community centres offer low-cost meals. Carnegie Community Centre is at 401 Main Street; Gathering Place is at 609 Helmcken Street; Evelyne Saller Centre is at 404 Alexander Street.

Evelyne Saller currently advertises $2 full-course meals. Menus, serving times, membership requirements and capacity can change, so check the City pages or call the centre before relying on a specific meal.
Community centres with additional supports — City of Vancouver
The City maintains lists and maps of free or low-cost groceries and meals. BC211 can search by neighbourhood, dietary need, age or household type.
Ask whether identification, registration, a referral, a container or early arrival is required. A published schedule can change without notice.
Free and low-cost resources — City of Vancouver

categories.title: 4. Showers, laundry, clothing, mail and internet

items.name: Evelyne Saller Centre — showers and laundry

content.text: Address:
404 Alexander Street
Phone:
. The City lists free showers and laundry, health supports, a low-cost cafeteria and free Wi-Fi for low-income and at-risk adults.
Capacity and service times are separate from building hours. Call or ask at the front desk about same-day sign-up before waiting.
Evelyne Saller Centre — City of Vancouver
Address:
609 Helmcken Street
Phone:
. Services include showers, laundry, washrooms, a reading room, education centre, low-cost cafeteria, free Wi-Fi and some clothing support.
Ask about membership or ID requirements and current sign-up times. Showers, laundry and clothing may reach capacity.
Gathering Place — City of Vancouver

items.name: Downtown Eastside Women's Centre — practical needs

content.text: Addresses:
302 Columbia Street and 25 East Hastings Street

Drop-in services for women include hot meals, free clothing, safe washrooms, showers, toiletries, menstrual products, a secure mailing address, phone and computer access, first aid and harm-reduction supplies.
Services and hours differ between the two sites. Phone
or check the location pages before going.
Drop-in centres — Downtown Eastside Women's Centre
Address:
1138 Burrard Street
Youth aged 13 to 24 can use washrooms, hot showers, laundry and lockers and may receive food, clothing, shoes, toiletries and harm-reduction supplies. The drop-in is open 24 hours.
Call or text:
. Ask staff about ID, mail, housing, health and employment help.
Directions Drop-In Centre
The City list includes The Door Is Open, Evelyne Saller Centre, Gathering Place, Lookout and RainCity locations. Clothing is subject to availability and some sites require membership or ID.
Call first if you need a specific size, footwear, work clothing, rain gear, blankets or menstrual products.
Clothing providers — City of Vancouver

items.name: Vancouver Public Library — internet and documents

content.text: Central Library:
350 West Georgia Street
The Central Library has computers, Wi-Fi, charging stations, printers, photocopiers and scanners. Scanning to email is free; printing has a charge.
Ask the Level 2 Service Desk about a free Library or Internet Access card. Ask staff about alternatives if you do not have standard identification.
Central Library
Printing and scanning

categories.title: 5. Health, mental health and substance use

content.text: Phone:
, 24 hours. A navigator can find local care and connect callers to a registered nurse for non-emergency symptoms. Translation is available in more than 130 languages.

Use 811 to ask about walk-in care, community clinics, mental-health services or medication questions. Call 911 for severe breathing trouble, chest pain, unconsciousness, major bleeding, overdose or another immediate threat to life.
HealthLink BC 811 services

items.name: Community health care without a regular doctor

content.text: Ask 811 or a shelter or outreach worker to find the appropriate Vancouver Coastal Health clinic. Explain if you have no fixed address, no phone, no valid health card, mobility needs or medication that may be lost or stolen.
Community health centres serve different areas and programs. Call first because many services require an appointment or have specific eligibility.
Vancouver mental-health and substance-use services — Vancouver Coastal Health

items.name: Insite — supervised consumption and health support

content.text: Address:
139 East Hastings Street

Vancouver Coastal Health's December 2025 map lists supervised injection from 9am to 2am daily and drug checking from 10am to 6pm. Staff can respond to overdose and connect people with health and treatment services.
Hours can change. Check the current Vancouver map before going. For an overdose already happening, call 911 and give naloxone if available.
Vancouver supervised consumption and overdose-prevention map — Vancouver Coastal Health

The current VCH map includes Powell Street Getaway, Overdose Prevention Society, Hope to Health, Molson, Astoria and Get Your Drugs Tested. Services differ: some support injection, some inhalation and some drug checking.
Use the map for exact addresses and hours. Do not use alone; carry naloxone when possible. Call 911 for a suspected overdose.
Current Vancouver harm-reduction sites — Vancouver Coastal Health
Access Central:
. Vancouver Coastal Health lists this referral line for services including Vancouver detox, Harbour Light Detox, Daytox and other substance-use supports.
A call does not guarantee same-day admission. Tell the navigator about withdrawal risk, pregnancy, medications, accessibility and whether you have somewhere safe to wait.
Harm-reduction and substance-use guide — Vancouver Coastal Health

PHS Community Services Society operates low-barrier primary care, dental, mental-health, addiction and harm-reduction services for people who face barriers to mainstream care in the Downtown Eastside.
Programs have different intake rules. Ask a PHS site, outreach worker, shelter worker or 811 which clinic fits your need and whether an appointment is required.
PHS Community Services Society

If there is immediate danger, a serious injury or someone cannot stay safe, call 911. For non-emergency mental-health care, call 811 and ask for a health navigator or contact City outreach, a shelter worker or a community clinic.
Say if you need a non-police option, interpretation, Indigenous cultural support, youth care or help related to substance use. Availability varies and an assessment may be required.
Mental-health supports — HealthLink BC
Phone:
. Apply through My Self Serve, by phone or at an income-assistance office. Tell the worker if you urgently need food, shelter or medical attention.

Vancouver offices include Dockside at 180 Main Street, Kiwassa at 205 Powell Street, Strathcona at 687 Powell Street and other neighbourhood locations. Offices normally close from noon to 1pm; confirm before going.
Apply for assistance
Office locations

items.name: If you do not have all required identification

content.text: Do not assume you cannot apply. Provincial policy allows temporary assistance in some cases while required ID is being pursued after identity has been verified.
Ask the intake worker what can be used in your case and request help from City outreach or a shelter worker to replace missing documents. Eligibility is assessed individually.
Identification requirements — Government of British Columbia
Lower Mainland:
Toll-free:
. Eligible low-income people, including single people or couples who are homeless or at risk, can apply.
The Housing Listings are not a vacancy list, and some buildings require a separate application directly to the provider. Apply to every suitable building and keep contact information updated.
Subsidized housing — BC Housing

City outreach at 392 Powell Street can help with housing applications and move-in steps. Shelter and community workers may also complete referrals or supporting forms when a program requires professional verification.
No worker can guarantee a unit or move-in date. Keep copies of applications, record building codes and report changes to your phone, mailing address or household.
Housing help through City outreach
Phone:
. The Vancouver Rent Bank may offer an interest-free loan for eligible low- to moderate-income renters facing a temporary crisis involving rent, utilities or a deposit.
It is a loan, not an automatic grant. Proof of tenancy, bank statements, income and identification are normally required, and the applicant must be able to cover ongoing costs and repayment.
Vancouver Rent Bank contact
Eligibility and application
The provincial program provides a subsidized annual pass to eligible low-income seniors and people receiving disability assistance. It works on TransLink but not on HandyDART or West Coast Express.
Apply or ask about eligibility:
. Being homeless by itself does not create eligibility; ask an assistance worker about other transport support.
BC Bus Pass Program
WorkBC offers free computers, internet, printing and scanning, job listings, résumé and interview help, workshops and one-to-one employment planning for eligible job seekers.
A downtown centre is at 200-250 West Pender Street,
. Other centres serve Burrard, Commercial Drive, East 3rd Avenue, Midtown West and South Vancouver. Call to confirm intake and hours.
WorkBC centre services and locations
Youth aged 13 to 24 can ask about employment workshops, job support, education, ID replacement and connections to training while using the 24-hour drop-in.
Call or text:
. Programs and workshop schedules change, so ask staff what is currently open.
Directions Youth Services
Address:
Vancouver Aboriginal Friendship Centre, 1607 East Hastings Street

The free Employment and Life Skills Training program is for people who self-identify as First Nations, Métis or Inuit. It offers employment workshops, short certifications, computer and transport support, food and work gear during training.
Contact the Friendship Centre at
to ask about intake and upcoming sessions.
Employment and Life Skills Training — VAFCS
Welcome Centre:
2610 Victoria Drive
Phone:
. Free programs can help eligible newcomers, refugee claimants and asylum seekers with settlement, English, job search and career planning.
Eligibility depends on immigration status and the specific program. Ask about BC SAFE HAVEN or the appropriate employment service.
Vancouver Welcome Centre — ISSofBC
Do not pay for a job offer, send money to an employer, deposit a cheque and return part of it, or share a SIN before a legitimate employer needs it for payroll.
Ask WorkBC to review a suspicious offer. Keep your SIN confidential and do not use it as general identification.
Protecting your SIN — Government of Canada
A SIN is needed to work in Canada and access some government programs. There is no fee to apply. Service Canada no longer issues plastic SIN cards.
SIN Program:
. Required documents depend on citizenship or immigration status. Ask a shelter or outreach worker for help scanning documents or arranging a safe mailing address.
Apply for a SIN — Government of Canada
A BCID is government photo identification for people who do not drive. An appointment, accepted identity documents and a fee are normally required at a driver licensing office.
Before paying or travelling, use the ICBC document checker. City outreach can help apply for or safely store identification and may identify help with replacement costs.
Apply for a BCID — ICBC

items.name: Benefits and tax mail without a permanent home

content.text: The Canada Revenue Agency says a person without a permanent home can use a temporary address, such as a shelter, to continue receiving payments and mail.

Ask the shelter or drop-in for permission before using its address. Check how often mail must be collected and what name or identification is required. Update each government department separately when the address changes.
CRA help for people experiencing housing insecurity
Greater Vancouver:
Elsewhere in BC:
. Legal Aid assesses eligibility for covered legal matters.
Have court papers, deadlines and available proof of income ready. If the matter is urgent, say the next hearing, eviction or response date at the start of the call.
Call Legal Aid BC
Phone:
. Advocates help with income assistance, disability benefits, Employment Insurance, employment standards, government debt, tenancy and related issues.
Drop-in intake times and the service location can change. Check the current page before going and bring notices, decisions, identification and deadlines if available.
Legal advocacy — FIRST UNITED

Contact a legal or tenant organization immediately after receiving an eviction notice. Do not ignore the notice; dispute deadlines can be short. FIRST UNITED and other organizations listed by the City can explain options.
The Vancouver Rent Bank may help with an eligible temporary financial crisis, but an application does not by itself stop an eviction. Keep copies of every notice, payment and message.
Renter supports and protections — City of Vancouver

Make a list of what is missing and contact each issuer. Ask City outreach, Directions, DEWC or another trusted worker to help with applications, fees, photocopies, secure storage and a mailing address.
Do not send original documents unless an official process specifically requires them. Record application numbers and keep digital copies in a secure account when possible.
Identification help — City outreach

categories.title: 9. Women, youth, Indigenous people, newcomers and 2SLGBTQIA+ people

content.text: Downtown Eastside Women's Centre offers low-barrier drop-in, meals, showers, clothing, mail, housing support, advocacy and victim services. Its 412 East Cordova shelter is open 24 hours.
WISH provides shelter and services for women and gender-diverse street-based sex workers. If violence or exploitation is involved, call or text VictimLinkBC at
Downtown Eastside Women's Centre
WISH Shelter
Directions is open 24 hours at 1138 Burrard Street for food, showers, laundry, lockers, health connections, ID help, employment support and an overnight shelter for ages 19 to 24.
Covenant House serves ages 16 to 24 with drop-in, crisis shelter and specialist programs. Call both providers if one program does not fit your age or needs.
Directions youth homelessness services
Covenant House
Reaching Home intake:
1015 East Hastings Street
Phone:
. VAFCS supports Indigenous people who are homeless or at risk with housing placement, financial assistance, case management, employment and cultural connection.
Hours are listed as Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. Funding and housing are not guaranteed; contact the intake worker to confirm eligibility and current capacity.
Reaching Home — Vancouver Aboriginal Friendship Centre Society
ISSofBC Welcome Centre:
2610 Victoria Drive
Phone:
. The centre provides free settlement, English, employment and referrals for housing, health, legal and family services in many languages.

BC SAFE HAVEN supports refugee claimants and asylum seekers with the claim process, settlement, English, job search, mental-health referrals and urgent accommodation search. Eligibility varies by program.
Vancouver Welcome Centre — ISSofBC
QMUNITY:
1170 Bute Street
Phone:
. QMUNITY offers peer groups, counselling, information and referrals, youth and older-adult services, and low-barrier legal help.
The current office is reached by 23 stairs; accessible meetings can be arranged on request. It is not an emergency shelter. Tell BC211, Directions or Covenant House where you feel safest.
QMUNITY programs and services
Contact and accessibility

Tell BC211 immediately if children are with you so the navigator can look for a family placement. BC Housing's current Vancouver list includes the Vi Fineday Family Shelter at 1906 West 15th Avenue, but intake and space must be confirmed.
Do not travel to a family shelter without checking the referral process. Mention pregnancy, child age, custody, accessibility, school and safety needs.
Current provincial Vancouver shelter list — BC Housing

items.name: Find a shelter that accepts pets

content.text: Use the pet-friendly filter on the BC211 shelter list and call the site before travelling. Ask about species, size, number of animals, crates, vaccination records and whether the animal stays with you.
Directions accepts youth with pets, and BC211 currently marks several adult shelters as pet-friendly. Capacity can change even when the general policy allows animals.
Pet-friendly shelter filter — BC211
Address:
543 Powell Street

The BC SPCA lists service every Tuesday from 11am to 1pm for homeless, outdoor, low-income and senior pet guardians in the Downtown Eastside. It distributes pet food and supplies and may offer nail trimming, grooming and training advice.
Animal Helpline:
. Call to confirm the schedule or ask about other pet-food locations.
Pet food bank — BC SPCA
The BC SPCA may offer short-term emergency boarding in situations such as hospitalization, interpersonal violence, fire or flood. Availability and eligibility are assessed.
Call the Animal Helpline before going. If leaving violence, also ask VictimLinkBC about pet-safe planning and the SPCA Safekeepers program.
BC SPCA community services

items.name: Winter shelters and Extreme Weather Response

content.text: Temporary winter shelters normally add spaces during the colder months. Extreme Weather Response sites open only when an alert is active. Criteria include cold, snow, freezing rain, severe wind and heavy rain.
Use the live BC211 list immediately before travelling. An address published for the winter does not mean the site is active or has space tonight.
Shelters and winter response — City of Vancouver
The City activates warming centres when the temperature reaches or feels like -4°C or below. These centres provide a warm indoor space but are not set up with beds or mats.
Activation locations are announced with extreme-weather alerts. Check the City shelter page, the BC211 list or ask a shelter or outreach worker before going.
Current winter response — City of Vancouver
During hot weather, City community centres and libraries provide air-conditioned spaces. No registration, payment or identification is required; seating, drinking water and washrooms are available.

Most community-centre cooling sites accept well-behaved pets, but Evelyne Saller and Carnegie do not, and pets are not allowed in library cooling centres. Check the current map and hours during a heat event.
Hot-weather resources — City of Vancouver
City facilities with cleaner air operate during their regular hours and may provide relief from smoke. Limit strenuous outdoor activity, drink water and carry prescribed rescue medication.
Call 811 for health advice. Call 911 for severe breathing trouble, chest pain, fainting or another immediate emergency.
Cleaner-air guidance — City of Vancouver

This page prioritizes current government pages, the live BC211 shelter list and providers' own websites. Shelter space, weather response, meal schedules and intake rules can change without notice. Confirm before travelling and report any incorrect detail.
